# Flow 2: the vessel's shell drifts, and the Captain reconciles it.
#
# The vessel needs a shell. It is a resource on the vessel like any other, recorded the first time
# a terminal loads Orbiter's profile line. Here the recorded shell's integration goes missing (as
# after copying a star chart to another machine), a scan flags it, and calibrate looks for shells
# through the installed integrations, shows what was found and what is missing, and lets the
# Captain choose.

step set up the vessel and let the terminal of the Captain register its shell
exec orbiter --output json vessel init -y
exec $FLOW_SHELL -c 'eval "$(orbiter shell init)"'

step the vessel has a shell on record
exec orbiter --output json survey vessel -v
stdout '"role":"shell"'

step the integration of the recorded shell goes missing
rm $HOME/.orbiter/integrations/$FLOW_SHELL

step a scan flags the drift: nothing is installed that can speak for the recorded shell
exec orbiter --output json scan vessel
stdout '"role":"shell"'
stdout '"status":"failed"'

step the Captain opens a terminal running a different shell
env SHELL=$FLOW_OTHER_SHELL_PATH

step calibrate shows what is missing and what was found; the client chooses the first shell offered
client -- calibrate vessel
stdout '"op":"SELECT"'
stdout 'has drifted: its integration folder is not in the integrations directory'
stdout 'Shells found by the integrations in the integrations directory: '

step the shell of the vessel is now the one the Captain chose, and the drifted one is gone
exec orbiter --output json survey vessel -v
stdout '"role":"shell"'
stdout '"brand":"'$FLOW_OTHER_SHELL'"'
! stdout '"brand":"'$FLOW_SHELL'"'


step the new shell has no recorded location yet: calibrate asks for discovery
client -- calibrate vessel
stdout '"status":"needs_discovery"'
stdout '"op":"FIND_BINARY","key":"'$FLOW_OTHER_SHELL'"'
capture SESSION '"session":"([0-9a-z]+)"'
capture TXN '"txn":"([0-9a-z]+)","op":"FIND_BINARY"'

step the terminal of the Captain now runs the shell Orbiter has on record, and answers the search with its own hook
# The hook comes from the shell integration Orbiter delegates to; nothing is detected this time.
exec $FLOW_OTHER_SHELL -c 'eval "$(orbiter shell init)"; FIND_BINARY "$TXN" '$FLOW_OTHER_SHELL

step uplink records the location and the shell of the vessel is healthy
# The shell integration checks its own health with a command its manifest declares, the same
# way every tool does; the host holds it to that declaration.
client -- uplink --session=$SESSION
stdout '"role":"shell"'
stdout '"action":"healthy"'
